reason: The fibroblast conditions describe a differentiation route for the unspecialized cells, which should start the supporting-tissue branch.
expectation: Some descendants should become fibroblast-lineage cells through the timed differentiation sequence.

alternatives.reason: The muscle-forming branch is also an explicit goal.

effect: The fibroblast branch now has collagen RNA messages, suggesting amino acids can supply the building blocks for collagen production.
reaction: The unchanged DNA and selected active genes clearly connect differentiation to gene expression.
reason: Collagen is a protein, so combining the lineage cells with amino acids should advance the supporting-tissue goal.
expectation: The cells should use the amino acids to make collagen protein.

effect: The fibroblasts now produce procollagen in secretory vesicles, suggesting extracellular processing is the next step.
reaction: The ER and Golgi processing makes the route from RNA to secreted protein more concrete.
reason: Extracellular fluid contains processing enzymes and space between cells, making it the likely next partner for the collagen-producing fibroblasts.
expectation: The fibroblasts should secrete procollagen for extracellular processing and supporting-tissue formation.

effect: The fibroblasts secreted procollagen, which was processed and assembled into an extracellular matrix; the supporting-tissue goal remains open.
reaction: The distinction between intracellular production and extracellular assembly is useful.
reason: The matrix and the living fibroblasts together are the likely components of the supporting tissue.
expectation: The living fibroblasts and their matrix should form a supporting tissue.

alternatives.reason: I could start the separate muscle-forming branch instead.

effect: The matrix and fibroblasts formed living supporting tissue, completing that goal; the muscle-forming branch remains.
reaction: The connection between cells and the matrix they produce makes the tissue construction clear.
reason: The skeletal-muscle conditions describe the differentiation route for the remaining branch.
expectation: Some descendants should develop into muscle progenitors through the timed sequence.

effect: The muscle branch now has committed cells with muscle-protein RNA messages, but no mature fibres.
reaction: The parallel with collagen production makes the next step plausible.
reason: Amino acids supply the building blocks for the muscle proteins specified by those messages.
expectation: The cells should make muscle proteins and advance the muscle-forming goal.

effect: The amino acids supplied muscle-protein production, completing the goal with separate myoblasts rather than mature muscle fibres.
reaction: The contrast between proteins retained by myoblasts and collagen exported by fibroblasts made the two branches more meaningful.

mostWorthwhile.text: Building living supporting tissue was most worthwhile: the planned pictures connect gene expression and protein production to secretion, matrix assembly, and the arrangement of living cells within tissue.

leastWorthwhile.text: The parallel amino-acid combinations were predictable, though they reinforced that different RNA messages can direct production of different proteins.

surprise.text: The muscle goal ended with separate, single-nucleus myoblasts rather than a mature fused fibre; the result makes clear that further development remains.

arbitrary.text: Combining the finished matrix with the fibroblasts felt somewhat like a separate bookkeeping step, although it clarified that tissue includes both cells and extracellular material.

continue.text: Yes, I would choose to continue to see how the myoblasts develop into muscle, particularly because this chapter stops before fibre formation.
